note: Every Cedwyn webapp is one of the 59 numbered parcels of the estate plan ("NN of 59"). Positions read from the plan are approximate; the rest are schematic until the plan is read at full resolution. No parcel shape is drawn until it is traced from a source.

h3.why: Resolution 11 (about 25 m edge, 0.2 ha) is the coarsest resolution at which all 59 parcel positions fall in 59 different cells; the whole estate sits in one resolution-7 cell. r10 and r9 are parent cells.
h3.computed_with: h3-js 4.1.0, offline; the cells are precomputed and no library is shipped

georef.plan: Estate survey plan of the parish of Llandough (numbered parcels 1-59; River Ely along the north; church and village at the south-east). Identified in research cycle E1 (18 Oct 2026) as probably the 1824 Bute estate survey by David Stewart, Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1, plan 19 "Cedfin alias Ty Mawr". Read from a 720x1600 screenshot; a higher-resolution copy is a research task.
georef.method: Similarity transform (scale, rotation, shift) fitted by least squares to 6 control points; plan pixels to metres east/north of 51.4525 N, 3.198 W.
